5218	## Owner statements 2026-11-12 — a robust base for every language, jurisdiction and term; parameters defined dynamically; a source is read once for every parameter; the pipeline runs in every direction
5219	
5220	Four statements made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:
5221	
5222	> "ensure that our pipeline can be run in all directions at any stage in such a manner where we can dynamically research, adjudicate, synthesize, specify and render across a multitude of languages and jurisdictions."
5223	
5224	> "ensure that we have a robust base for languages/jurisdictions/terms/etc so that we can leverage all of them for comprehensive research, and ensure that we can dynamically derive/define new parameters as well as find linkages and equivalencies and clauses in order to group things as much as possible for clarity and robustness"
5225	
5226	> "ensure that whenever we read a source we are able to derive all information relevant to all parameters we have defined in our base so that we don't have to repeatedly read a source to get values or worry about missing it"
5227	
5228	> "Fable has permission to design, author, curate, orchestrate, delete as required to ensure code pipeline works as desired" — confirmed on the assistant's reading (code, schema, scripts, checks and skills; doctrine stays owner-gated) — and, later, "Fable allowed to curiously stress test, patch and iterat[e]".
5229	
5230	**What this records.**
5231	1. **Objective.** The pipeline is to be runnable in every direction from any stage, dynamically, across many languages and jurisdictions. This was an unrecorded objective in the top-down audit ledger (C-17).
5232	2. **Base.** Languages, jurisdictions, terms and the rest of the base are to be a robust substrate that research can use in full, new parameters are to be derivable or definable dynamically, and linkages, equivalencies and clauses are to be found and used to group, for clarity and robustness.
5233	3. **Read once.** A source read is to yield everything relevant to every parameter defined in the base, so no source is re-read for values and nothing is missed. This restates, and does not replace, the 2026-10-09 statement that every source is scanned for every parameter and OR-11a's full-scope scan.
5234	4. **Authority.** A Fable implementation agent may design, author, curate, orchestrate, delete, stress test, patch and iterate on the code pipeline, within the rules that bind code (migrations only for the database, tooling and research rows in separate PRs, scratch copies for stress tests). Mission, audience, CRPD posture, population taxonomy, evidence-tier definitions, jurisdiction scope, licensing and trajectory remain the owner's. [ASSUMPTION: the grant covers the code pipeline and not doctrine — the owner answered "Assumption is correct" to this reading.]
5235	
5236	**What it does not decide.** What "render across languages" means, whether a determination varies by jurisdiction, and how a parameter added after a source was read is applied to that source (re-read, or retained text) are open and are `OWNER DECISION REQUIRED` items in the audit's improvement programme.
5237	
5238	CONDITION: any session asking what the pipeline's omnidirectional, multilingual, multijurisdictional or read-once objectives are, or what authority the implementation agent holds.
5239	ACTION: (1) Treat the three objective statements as live requirements on the pipeline. (2) Do not re-read a source to extract a parameter that the source's earlier full-scope reading already covered; where a parameter postdates the reading, a catalogue-growth route must exist and is owed. (3) Implement under the authority in item 4 and no wider. (4) Treat the doctrine questions above as the owner's.
5240	DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statements, quoted above.

5243	## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (second) — parameters are approached from a higher, abstract vantage so that commonality survives and can be unified, then specified
5244	
5245	Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:
5246	
5247	> "recognize that we need to approach parameters from a higher level abstract vantage as too many clauses and subclauses means we may lose commonality and therefore can't unify then specify"
5248	
5249	**What this records.** The grain at which a parameter is defined is to be abstract enough that clauses and subclauses from different instruments and jurisdictions remain comparable; defined too finely, the commonality is lost and nothing can be unified, so nothing can be specified. The order named is unify, then specify.
5250	
5251	**What it does not decide.** How the abstraction is represented (a parent/child or family relation, an equivalence group, a coarser parameter list), who judges a grouping, and how clause-level traceability is kept under a coarser parameter are open. It touches the 2026-08-26 ruling that the judgment object is the canonical parameter and the 2026-10-09 statement that the parameter list is seeded from the existing terms; neither is superseded by this entry. Whether a granularity policy is doctrine (owner-gated) or a tooling convention is `OWNER DECISION REQUIRED` in the audit's improvement programme. [ASSUMPTION: "higher level abstract vantage" is read as a change of grain for parameters, not as permission to discard clause-level extractions.]
5252	
5253	CONDITION: any session defining, splitting, merging or grouping parameters, or asking why a determination cannot be unified across instruments.
5254	ACTION: (1) Treat commonality across clauses, instruments and jurisdictions as a property a parameter definition must preserve. (2) Keep clause-level extractions and reach them from an abstract parameter by pointer. (3) Do not decide the grouping mechanism or the granularity policy without the owner. (4) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
5255	DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statement, quoted above.
5256

5259	
5260	Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), directly after the second statement of the same day, recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:
5261	
5262	> "so our synthesis needs to be very dynamic in finding equivalencies/adjacencies/similarities/commonalities so that it can discuss things properly"
5263	
5264	**What this records.** The synthesis stage is the one that finds the relations between parameters, clauses, instruments and jurisdictions (equivalence, adjacency, similarity, commonality) and does so dynamically, as a request needs it, in order that the book's discussion is sound. It is the step that makes the abstraction in the second statement usable: unify, then specify.

5266	**What it does not decide.** The relation types, their representation, who judges them, and how a dynamic run is initiated are open. It does not change the rule that only an Opus-class model authors `best_practice_synthesis`. [ASSUMPTION: "synthesis" is read as the pipeline stage of that name, not as `best_practice_synthesis` alone.]

38	### 1.3 The agonist–antagonist method
39	
40	- **Agonist.** Writes the document as numbered positions (`P-<doc>-<n>`): one claim or proposal each, with its evidence and status mark. The agonist files the complete affirmative case; nothing is held back for a reply.
41	- **Antagonist.** A separate context that has not read the agonist's working, only the draft and the sources. It attacks each position through named lenses: **existence** (does the cited thing exist at the cited place today), **fidelity** (does the quote or row say what the position says), **supersession** (is a later ruling in the way), **subject** (did the cited check examine anything; a zero-row object is unproven), **count** (is any number typed), **warrant class** (owner quote, ledger reading, contract, relayed, memory note, assumption), **assumption import**, **owner gate** (is something decided that is the owner's), **redness** (could the proposed test fail on today's data; run it), **prior work** (does an existing plan already say this). The antagonist must re-run at least the commands this brief lists for the document, before reading the agonist's figures, and then compare (blind, then compare).
42	- **Resolution record.** The last section of every document, one row per position: `position | antagonist objection (lens) | evidence for the objection | disposition`. Dispositions: `upheld` (objection failed; say why), `amended` (text changed; say how), `withdrawn`, `referred to owner` (becomes or joins an OD entry). Positions the antagonist attacked and could not fault are recorded as `upheld — attacked on <lenses>`; a record that shows only sustained objections is incomplete.
43	- **One round.** No reply to the antagonist, no pass on the pass. Disputes go to the owner register.

Given in session https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iQ3vbthbsh45LNks6j, in reply to prompts OR-1, OR-2, OR-3, OR-5 and OR-6 of the owner's browser page (`workplan/2026-10-23-pipeline-resolution-workplan.md` section 4; the decision sheet of the 2026-10-22 resolution report), and recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0 and workplan WR-3. OR-1:

> "A parameter does not require a lens for each and every disability population or access need. Do not store table rows for parameters when there is a missing lens for a disability population or access need, i.e. for when the parameter is not relevant. In other words, I expect each and every determination to only have rows for the actual relevant lens. Ensure that all relevant codes/identification/lenses are filled out as required, i.e. a determination should never be limited to only one lens because we have different models for discussing disability (ICF, population identity, access needs)--we need to have each model filled out accordingly."

> "Co-1 figures may set a value insofar as the source is academically sound. Otherwise, they set the direction, not the number."

OR-6:

groups — are **not** covered by either new code and remain owed. Balance-demand users likewise. The
schema work must therefore be built to extend, not to close.

**Why the split was owed, in the project's own terms.** `MOB` — *"disabled people with mobility
needs; wheelchair users"*, described as *"General mobility limitation including walking, balance, or
wheeled mobility"* — fails clause **(c)** of the ratified permitted-umbrella test (2026-07-23):
*"no opposed demand between members."* Ramp gradient is opposed between its members (a manual
wheelchair user wants a shallower gradient; an ambulant person with fatigue or spasticity often
wants a shorter run, and therefore a steeper one), and handrails serve ambulant and balance users
first while obstructing some wheeled users. The test that forbids this umbrella has existed since
2026-07-23; `MOB` was never run through it.

Not refused, by design: a finding row added to the parameter after the answer (research goes on, and K02 reports it), a data migration, and the verification cron. Those, and any route nobody has thought of, are noticed afterwards by `assess_cell.stale_determinations`, which `derivation_handshake_integrity` runs: it re-runs the engine on each live determination of the current `RULE_VERSION` and compares the stored answer. Like K01 and K02 it examines nothing while no determination is live; `scripts/tests/test_assess_cell_pilot.py` exercises it on a fixture. Re-derive the columns the engine reads: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts'); import dbcore; print(dbcore.ENGINE_SOURCE_COLUMNS, dbcore.ENGINE_EXTRACTION_COLUMNS)"`.

def stale_determinations(conn):
    """The live determinations this engine wrote (`RULE_VERSION`) whose stored answer is no longer
    the one `determine` gives, as (specification_id, [the fields that differ]).

    THE STORED MARKER IS A CACHE. It is read off the sources' verification and tier, the rows'
    grading and comparators, and the `confirms` edges, and `derivation_sha` hashes none of them
    (K01 verifies only the stored junction, K02 only that it is complete). `db.py` refuses the
    routes it knows (a regrading, an edge, a source's engine-read columns); a data migration, the
    verification cron or a route not yet thought of does not pass through it. This is what
    notices, whichever route moved the input. The remedy is the one the refusals name: retire the
    specification, re-determine."""
    cols = ("specification_id", "parameter_id", *LENS_ORDER, *STORED_ANSWER)
    out = []
    for sid, pid, *rest in conn.execute(
            f"SELECT {', '.join(cols)} FROM specifications WHERE retired_at IS NULL "
            f"AND rule_version = ? ORDER BY specification_id", (RULE_VERSION,)).fetchall():
        lens = dict(zip(LENS_ORDER, rest))
        det = determine(conn, pid, lens, "", "recomputed")
        diff = [f for f, was in zip(STORED_ANSWER, rest[len(LENS_ORDER):]) if det[f] != was]
        if diff:
            out.append((sid, diff))
    return out

def vacuity_failure(check, output):
    """A check that examined nothing has not passed — it has abstained.

    `validate_schema` was BLOCKING and named six data/ subdirectories that have
    never existed. It found zero files, printed "No entity files found to
    validate." and exited 0, so the entity-schema gate reported green for its
    whole life while examining nothing. That is worse than no gate, because it is
    counted as coverage.

    Opt-in per check via `min_items:` in the registry, because some corpora are
    legitimately empty. A declared check must print `EXAMINED: <n>`; if it does
    not, that is itself the failure — an unverifiable count cannot be trusted to
    be non-zero. Deliberately a FAIL and not a SKIP: SKIP is excluded from the
    verdict even at blocking level, which would hide exactly what this catches.
    """
    minimum = check.get("min_items")
    if not minimum:
        return None
    if not isinstance(minimum, int) or isinstance(minimum, bool) or minimum < 1:
        # C8 rejects these at registration; this is the runtime backstop, because
        # `min_items: "lots"` used to reach the `seen < minimum` comparison below
        # and raise TypeError, aborting the entire run and losing every check
        # after the offending one. A malformed floor is a registry defect, so it
        # is reported as a failure of the check that declares it — never a crash,
        # and never a silent pass.
        return (f"declares a malformed min_items ({minimum!r}); a floor must be a "
                "positive integer, so this check's vacuity guard is not armed")
    match = EXAMINED_RE.search(output or "")
    if not match:
        return (f"declares min_items={minimum} but printed no 'EXAMINED: <n>' line, "
                "so the number of items it looked at cannot be established")
    seen = int(match.group(1))
    if seen < minimum:
        return (f"examined {seen} item(s), below the declared minimum of {minimum} — "
                "the check passed by having nothing to look at")
    return None


    failures, errors, skips, vacuous = [], [], [], []
    floor_claims = []
    no_floor_kinds = reg.get("no_floor_kinds") or {}
    for check in active:
        if args.github:
            print(f"::group::{check['id']}")
        status, elapsed, output = run_check(check, session, env, args.github)
        line = report_line(check, status, elapsed)
        level = check.get("level", "blocking")

        if args.github:
            print(output)
            print("::endgroup::")
            print(line)
        else:
            print(line)
            if status in ("FAIL", "ERROR"):
                for tail in output.splitlines()[-8:]:
                    print(f"         {tail}")
            elif status in ("SKIP", "NONE"):
                print(f"         {output.splitlines()[-1] if output else 'skipped'}")

        claim = floor_claim_contradiction(check, output, no_floor_kinds)
        if claim:
            floor_claims.append((check["id"], level, claim[0], claim[1]))
            if args.github and claim[0] == "STALE":
                print(f"::error::{check['id']} declares no_floor over a non-empty subject")

        if status == "SKIP":
            skips.append(check["id"])
        elif status == "NONE":
            vacuous.append((check["id"], level))
            if args.github:
                print(f"::notice::{check['id']} examined nothing ({level}) — "
                      f"clean, but not coverage")
        elif status == "ERROR":
            errors.append((check["id"], level))
        elif status == "FAIL":
            failures.append((check["id"], level))
            if args.github:
                sev = "error" if level == "blocking" else "warning"
                print(f"::{sev}::{check['id']} failed ({level})")

    # --- verdict ------------------------------------------------------------
    # A contradicted floor claim fails AT THE DECLARING CHECK'S OWN LEVEL, not as a

## 5. Pull requests, in merge order

Procedure for each is the report §3 (tooling) or §4 (data). "Code" is the report's Appendix D estimate of net non-test lines (an estimate; measure with `git diff --shortstat origin/main -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations' ':!scripts/tests'`). The T-1 to T-8 estimates sum to roughly 650–935 net non-test lines (each figure already nets the deletions Appendix D counts for it).

**H-0 Ledger entry** (docs only). Appends the owner's answers (§4) and the §1 statement. A ruling that supersedes a ratified text also needs the audit's grammar (`scripts/audit/supersession_backpointer_audit.py`): a `SUPERSEDES: <target> :: "<quote>"` / `BY:` pair in the entry, **and** a one-line SUPERSEDED or AMENDED mark carrying the BY quote at the target, so H-0 edits those targets (report §7.3 lists them); a mark in `decisions/` needs an attestation (rule 2). OR-10's target is the ledger itself, where the pair cannot be written (ledger entry of 2026-10-20), so that supersession is stated in the entry's prose only. Also adds the derived owner queue to `.claude/commands/orient.md` (report §5, E12: open gates, open follow-ups, catalogue names awaiting approval, unadjudicated observations; text only, no apparatus). Opens only after the owner has answered; T-1a and T-6a do not wait for it.

**T-1a Reading** (report T-1, steps 1–7). Needs nothing. Resolves Q3, E2, Q2-assembly (derived arithmetic), Q13-trust (half); closes GAP-056 (the row closes in D-1).
Moves the notation arithmetic to `dbcore`; deletes `parse_bound` (dead) and the duplicate arithmetic in `derive_extraction`; the writer refuses unreadable figures, prose units, a missing comparator, and a derived figure that contradicts its inputs. Includes the numeral gloss (`--verbatim-exempt` cannot stand in for it: it is refused when the quote occurs in the bytes, and row 80's does).
*Done when:* N1–N11 pass; `test_assess_cell_pilot.py` passes; `extraction_relations_integrity.py` prints `VERDICT: CLEAN` with `EXAMINED:` above 0; `grep -rn "def parse_bound" scripts` is empty; `fixtures_g1_g13.py` output is byte-identical before and after; M1–M5 print KILLED; `build_graph.py --check` reports 0 failures. Code +45..95 net of the deletions it makes (Appendix D).

**T-6a Case fold** (report T-6 steps 1–2). Needs nothing. Resolves the language-label split (Q10-coverage). `log-search` folds and shape-checks the language; the coverage views fold with `UPPER()`; no UPDATE of history.
*Done when:* the C6 test that `log-search --language fr` stores `FR` and `--language xx1` is refused passes (the two `--term` tests belong to T-6b); `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT language) FROM v_coverage_language` equals `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT UPPER(language)) FROM search_executions WHERE deferred_reason IS NULL` (the view reads non-deferred rows only; the report's all-rows comparison is equal today only because no language is deferred-only); M20 KILLED. Code +50..80 across T-6.

**T-2 Conditions** (report T-2). Needs T-1a; OR-2. Resolves Q4, Q5 (mechanism), Q8 (conditionals), Q2-cross (the edge is how one parameter checks another). Governing rows with an outgoing `condition_on` edge leave the headline and become branches; a new such edge from a governing row of a live determination is refused. Reads only edges **from** governing rows (K-11).
*Done when:* B1–B6 pass; M7, M8 KILLED; C20's governing-edge query prints 0 before and after; fixture output unchanged; parameter 3 under MOB still reads `max 5.0`. Code +35..50.

**T-3 Lens** (report T-3). Needs T-2; OR-1, OR-1b. Resolves Q7, Q9, the pending-path defect. A row reaches a cell only through the lens codes written on it; the attestation hashes all four lens columns; a pending cell claims no derivation path; a NULL lens column can be filled with warrant.
*Done when:* L1–L5 and the amend tests pass; M9–M12 KILLED; K01 and K02 print PASS with a non-zero subject count on a populated scratch; no row is stored for a lens no figure carries (AUT, BLIND, ADHD, d450 and A-EFFORT on parameter 3 have no cell, per the ruling on OR-1), an identity-ALL figure reaches only an ALL determination (OR-1b), and how a determination and its figures carry several codes of one model is settled by OR-1c before this PR opens; (MOB) and (MOB, d450) differ in `derivation_sha`. Code +55..85.

**T-4 Agreement** (report T-4). Needs T-1a, T-3; OR-4, OR-5, OR-6, OR-6b. Resolves Q1, E8, E13, E6 (spread text). Excluded rows name their true cause; unsatisfiable anchors are recorded `divergent` and refuse to be written without a synthesis approach (WR-5), which for a T1 figure against a T2 figure is the owner's: the T1 figure is stated and the T2 dispute is noted in the item's discussion (ledger, OR-6; its reach is OR-6c); a Co-1 figure sets a value only when its source is academically sound (ledger, OR-5; how that is established is OR-5b), and otherwise sits beside the value, not in it; the note says how many rows set the selected bound.
*Done when:* the G1–G4, G8, G12, G13 assertions pass; the F-tests (report §6.1: every governing value × 1.1 and × 0.9, each comparator flipped, expectations written beside each case; the factor lives only in the test) pass; M13–M16 KILLED; `test_evidence_cell_state_2_3.py` and `validate_evidence_state.py` pass; §6.4's mechanism sentence is gone and any atom quoting it re-verifies (`verify_atoms.py`). Code +85..125. No tolerance, no engine-written approach (K-4, K-5).

**T-1b Optional reading steps**, each its own small PR on its ruling. Step 8 (OR-3): widens `amend-extraction` to unit, value and NULL `setting`; **must merge before D-1 if OR-3 is yes**. Step 9 (OR-10): the length family; bumps `RULE_VERSION`. Step 10 (OR-11a): the `verified` gate; its reader is T-5. *Done when:* N12 and M6 (step 8); `('36','in','>=')` reads `(Fraction(4572,5), None)` (step 9); for step 10, a test the report cites ("T-1 step 10 test") but does not define: `insert_extraction` and `amend_extraction` refuse `verified` without a full-scope `source_scans` row covering the row's parameter and accept it with one [GAP: write that test].

**T-5 Render** (report T-5, plan step 3.R). Needs T-2, T-3, T-4; OR-7, OR-11b. Resolves Q0, Q8 (render), E4 (the `insufficient` and `exceeds` edges only; see §9), E6, E7 (handoff), E10. Redefines `v_best_practice` (a T6-only cell appears, flagged), adds `v_determination_branches` and `v_code_inadequacy`, and adds `scripts/generate/render_cells.py`, which reads `specifications` directly so pending cells are not lost. Output goes to `$TMPDIR`; no rendered file is committed. **[Re-opened by the ruling on OW-1 (ledger, "Owner rulings 2026-10-29 (third)"): the render stage is expected to hold a table of complete prose and bibliographic information built from specifications and the preceding tables, so T-5's design waits on OW-1b and OW-1c.]**
## 6. What this plan declines

Report §7.1 (K-1 to K-14) is the list; each has its instead. Those most likely to be retried: traversing the crossing maps for lens routing (K-1); columns for conditions, branches, spread or selected bound (K-2); seeding from the old Part 4 index (K-3); a divergence tolerance or a percent sensitivity in code (K-4); an engine-written synthesis approach (K-5); a parity check between `extraction_status` and `source_scans` (K-8); backfilling `evidence_sources.language` (K-9); `UPDATE` of `search_executions` (K-10); `run_checks.py --all` to re-confirm (K-14). Also not built: a `claimed_unit` CHECK (Appendix A, finding 18), `search_indices` unless OR-9 names indices, per-lens direction (OR-21), cross-parameter synthesis tables (R17).

## 7. Order dependencies and the unknowns

Report §7.2 holds the order that breaks if sequenced wrongly; the one-line forms: T-2 before T-1a, T-5 before T-2 to T-4, D-1 before T-1a, D-2 before T-3, S-1 before D-1, two `RULE_VERSION` bumps in parallel branches, and a data PR open beside a tooling PR that changes the blob. The unknowns (report §8, U-1 to U-10) each name what settles them; U-4 is an owner or doctrine question with no command, and U-7 is OW-1 (§4).

## 8. Done

This plan is finished when all of these hold, each by its command:

1. T-1a to T-5 and T-8 are merged, and T-6a and T-6b, and T-7 if OR-14 is yes.
2. D-1 to D-5 and D-8 are merged, and D-6 and D-7 if their tooling is.
3. S-1 has rendered the live cells to `$TMPDIR`, with branches, code floors, flags and gaps present for the cells that have them.
4. The owner's battery (§9) is re-asked and every row's proof is green, or its last column names the ruling or limit that keeps it open.
5. The regression script (WR-4) shows every difference expected by §5 and none other.
6. `python3 workplan/pipeline-state-graph/walkability.py data/guidebook.db` prints no `NO PATH` line in either zigzag section (declared and populated). Today the only such lines are the ten `*<->render` lines (five pairs, each in both sections). Any pair that prints NO PATH after S-1 is named in S-1's record with its cause, and the owner rules it a residual. The directional matrix (up, down, skip, recvFK, sendFK) is reported with it, and no cell falls below its value at H-0; its zeros between research and the later stages are structural (no foreign key joins them) and are not a criterion. If OW-1 is no, the render lines stay and are named residuals.
7. Whether item 6 is a gate is OW-2. If yes, a registry entry runs `walkability.py` and fails on item 6; if no, item 6 is a command run at the end of each phase (simplification plan 4.4 says the same of it).
8. The aggregate change is measured (`git diff --shortstat <the commit before H-0>..origin/main -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'`) and reported to the owner with each PR's exception text. This plan does not promise it falls: the deletions available are those the PRs name, and step 4.4's is conditional (§2).

content.content:
RULE: The mobility split is ratified as `AMB` / `WHEEL`, and the 31 links fan out to both. Owner
ruling 2026-08-25: *"yes, AMB and WHEEL to fan out."* Settles the two questions the split design
(`scratchpad/…/logs/F5-population-split-design.md`) put to the owner.

**The codes.** `AMB` — ambulatory disabled people. `WHEEL` — wheelchair users, in the owner's own
wording and already the repository's person-term. `MOB` is superseded.

**The fan-out.** All **31** `item_population_links` rows keyed `MOB` (28 plain + 3
`with-upper-limb-involvement`, across 28 items) become **62** rows — one `AMB` and one `WHEEL` per
original — carrying each original's fields verbatim. The 31 originals are deleted. Net 372 → 403.

**What the fan-out asserts, stated plainly so it is not mistaken for a finding.** It is a
**mechanical carry of the umbrella's union**, not a judgement that every demand applies equally to
both. It is the anti-erasure choice: the alternative — resolving each of the 31 by hand now — would
decide applicability by inference, before synthesis, which is what `DR-2026-08-24` §2.4 forbids.
Every fanned row is therefore **pending synthesis re-derivation**, and the migration header must say
so. The 3 `with-upper-limb-involvement` rows are flagged for review rather than guessed.

**Not fanned out, ever:** `evidence_population_match.study_population` is free text describing *the
study's own* participants. A grade is a fact about a paper. (Moot in practice — measured **0** MOB
rows there — but recorded because the next split will not be moot.)

DATE: 2026-08-25 — owner ruling, quoted above.

---

RULE: The judgment object is the **canonical parameter**, and `items` is the render rollup the entity
model already calls it. Owner ruling 2026-08-26, selecting "key on the canonical parameter" from the
options put on the still-open question the grain ruling of 2026-08-25 left named and undecided —
*"what the judgment object is called"*, the owner's own parenthesis *"(if we use the word item)"*.

# C10 — a published cell may not rest on a source that has not been
    # established as real and usable.
    #
    # CORRECTED 2026-08-02, same day it was written. The first version tested
    # data_capture_status='pending' and failed 13 of 13 cells. That was wrong,
    # and wrong in an instructive way: capture-pending means "no row in an
    # extraction table", NOT "unread". All 59 sources cited by published cells
    # are VERIFIED or DISPUTED with COMPLETE metadata, and every cell carries a
    # convergence_id and tier_basis — they were plainly read. A cell cannot
    # precede the reading that produced it, so a well-formed cell is itself
    # evidence its sources were read, and the first version could only ever
    # have fired on a fabricated cell.
    #
    # Read-ness is recorded in verification_status, not in capture status. That
    # is what this now tests. DISPUTED counts as a failure: a best practice
    # resting on a source whose standing is contested is exactly the case worth
    # surfacing. (The old note here counted 2 DISPUTED among 59; D-0157
    # retired that status and no governing ref has ever been one.)
    # D-0157: a published cell may rest only on a source whose standing is
    # VERIFIED. The old list admitted VERIFIED-2 -- corroborated but never
    # obtained -- as sound; the remap moved those 71 rows to UNVERIFIED, so this
    # narrowing is the same judgement applied consistently rather than a new one.
    OK_VSTATUS = ("VERIFIED",)
    try:
        ph = ",".join("?" * len(OK_VSTATUS))
        unsound = conn.execute(f"""
            SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.specification_id)
            FROM specifications c
            -- THE JUNCTION, not json_each over the retired copy. `governing_refs` is
            -- NULL on every row written after the 2026-09-21 writer-retire, and
            -- json_each(NULL) yields NO ROWS -- so this BLOCKING gate would have
            -- examined nothing and passed green over exactly the cells it exists to
            -- catch. CLAUDE.md 5(a), a gate that passes having examined nothing.
            JOIN specification_source_links j
              ON j.specification_id = c.specification_id AND j.role = 'governing'
            JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = j.ref_id
            WHERE c.state IN ('stated','provisional')
              AND c.retired_at IS NULL
              AND COALESCE(e.verification_status,'') NOT IN ({ph})""",
            OK_VSTATUS).fetchone()[0]
        total_cells = conn.execute("""SELECT COUNT(*) FROM specifications
            WHERE state IN ('stated','provisional')
              AND retired_at IS NULL""").fetchone()[0]
        record("C10", "no published cell rests on an unverified or disputed source",
               unsound == 0,
               f"{unsound} of {total_cells} published cells cite a source that is "
               f"not verified (disputed, unverified, or no status)"
               if unsound else "",
               subject=total_cells)
    except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
        record("C10", "no published cell rests on an unverified or disputed source",
               False, f"could not evaluate: {exc}", subject=None)

    # C07 — a value column must hold a value, not a state written as prose.

**No. The audit is not accurate enough to build a plan suite on as it stands.** Its measurements of the database are sound (every section-Z query and every engine figure I re-ran reproduced), and its owner quotations of 2026-11-12 are exact. 40	### 1.3 The agonist–antagonist method
41	
42	- **Agonist.** Writes the document as numbered positions (`P-<doc>-<n>`): one claim or proposal each, with its evidence and status mark. The agonist files the complete affirmative case; nothing is held back for a reply.
43	- **Antagonist.** A separate context that has not read the agonist's working, only the draft and the sources. It attacks each position through named lenses: **existence** (does the cited thing exist at the cited place today), **fidelity** (does the quote or row say what the position says), **supersession** (is a later ruling in the way), **subject** (did the cited check examine anything; a zero-row object is unproven), **count** (is any number typed), **warrant class** (owner quote, ledger reading, contract, relayed, memory note, assumption), **assumption import**, **owner gate** (is something decided that is the owner's), **redness** (could the proposed test fail on today's data; run it), **prior work** (does an existing plan already say this). The antagonist must re-run at least the commands this brief lists for the document, before reading the agonist's figures, and then compare (blind, then compare).
44	- **Resolution record.** The last section of every document, one row per position: `position | antagonist objection (lens) | evidence for the objection | disposition`. Dispositions: `upheld` (objection failed; say why), `amended` (text changed; say how), `withdrawn`, `referred to owner` (becomes or joins an OD entry). Positions the antagonist attacked and could not fault are recorded as `upheld — attacked on <lenses>`; a record that shows only sustained objections is incomplete.
45	- **One round.** No reply to the antagonist, no pass on the pass. Disputes go to the owner register.
46	- **Finish.** A document is finished when its acceptance criteria (per document, below) hold and its resolution record has no position without a disposition.

**Verdict: yes — the amended audit is accurate enough to build the suite on.** All four blocking objections are resolved in text I re-ran and found true. Five material and seventeen minor inaccuracies remain; none is blocking.

**File written (only this one):** `/home/user/guidebook/scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/fa-confirmation.md`

**What I confirmed on the points you named**
- **Redesigned IMP-04:** it turns no registered check red and changes no `EXAMINED:` token. I ran the four checks from their registry commands and passed the real output, with one added live/retired line, through `run_checks`' three decision functions: PASS before and after on all four. I did not run `run_checks.py` itself.
- **C10 and R-6:** only parameters 3 and 12 determine `provisional` today, and both fail `test_db_integrity` C10. The R-6 query returns the four named sources on a parameter 3 copy.
- **IMP-05:** nothing with a reader is ordered deleted there any more; the cited readers are as stated.
- **Withdrawals:** every remaining reference to IMP-11, OD-16 and AT-56 states the withdrawal. IMP-16 has one remnant (AT-76, below).
- **OD-14 and OD-04:** the quoted ledger lines are exact.
- **OD-26 (the item referred to the owner):** it exists and is correctly stated.
- **Sonnet brief:** every prescribed command runs as written (the verb-list command returns 72), line references resolve, and the reserved id ranges do not collide with IMP-40, OD-26 or R-6.
- **Handshake table:** no verdict moved between `4afe1dd` and `756e6bf`.

**Inaccuracies, ranked**

Material:
1. **HS-3 IMP-12 still orders "Then DELETE `gap_mining`, its verbs and audit"** while it sits in the "doable now" set and IMP-05 makes that deletion a candidate behind a caller sweep. Unswept callers include the registry entry `gap_mining_audit`, `test_run_pipeline_refusals.py`, `graph/topology.py` and the `gap-driven-mining` skill.
2. **`fa-corrections-for-suite.md` §4 is incomplete.** Its eight items point at 11 of the 28 changed-claim rows plus §2. It omits C-03 (the IMP-04 and AT-54 change from blocking FA-01), C-07, C-10, C-14, C-15, C-19 and C-20, among others.
3. **HS-3 AT-53 was not restated.** It still tests "exits non-zero when a path that exists is removed", which IMP-07 now says is not the ruled gate, and still cites a grep count.
4. **HS-3 IMP-40 and §0 item 1 attribute an order to the ledger that it does not state.** PS:4934 gives the table's shape to "the tooling PR"; PS:4938 says T-3 and D-2 "can be designed, as a tooling pull request first". Neither puts a link-table pull request before T-3. The workplan's condition, "settled by OR-1c", is already met. A separate IMP-40 before T-3 is the handshake leg's sequencing.
5. **HS-3 IMP-10, HS-2 F-18 and C-10 say the repository already seeds "the other defects".** One of the five has no seeded test: a retired row surfaced by a view. This traces to my own FA-08 wording, which went further than my evidence.

Minor:
- **Count that does not fit:** "four governing sources" is the reason for parameter 3; the parameter 12 cell fails on one.
- **Gate inconsistency:** IMP-03a is ungated while OD-18 still asks about the same entry strings.
- **Remnants of withdrawn items:** AT-76 still reads "For: IMP-16"; HS-1 REQ-019 still calls the id collision a defect; C-08 says AT-20 loses its improvement, but IMP-39 still carries it.
- **Stale sentences in HS-2:** line 22 says only the four `hs-*` files were written; §4 still lists `test_db_integrity` as not run.
- **Corrections file:** C-17 says both verb-list commands are in §5, which holds only the results; C-04's affected-id list omits IMP-12, IMP-32 and IMP-36; §3 "Restated" omits OD-23.
- **Typed figures:** HS-1 §7 says "three governance files" where its command returns four; "20 with a text-extraction record" is right, but the cited command prints 23 as written.
- **Brief:**
  - "four rounds" where five steps are now listed, and document 7's reserved additions have no folding round.
  - "three permitted searches" against a fourth it prescribes over `sessions/`.
  - Document 2 still points at `queue`, not `decisions`.
  - Document 3 omits the 9 × `MOB` run that AT-51 needs.
  - Document 4's "Waves 0–2" scope no longer matches HS-3 §3.
  - Three warrant labels are off: "the owner's 'yes'", and PS:4693 and PS:4546 cited as owner lines.
  - PS:4761 is paraphrased as "until a render view exists" where it says "once the views key … has landed".

**Unverifiable:** whether a view mapped to render gives the render pairs a path; the instrument has no `views:` support yet.

**Not checked:** whether the workplan order T-1a → T-2 → T-3 is technically forced (the amended files correctly say it is taken from the workplan and untested). `add-alias` and `add-source` were read, not exercised.
